question: When several cases of loose motions are reported from one lane of a village, the first step of the community nurse is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. visit the houses, take the history of each case, examine the patients and inspect the source of drinking water

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The nurse finds out how many are ill, what they ate and drank and where the water comes from, and it is this information that shows the common source of the outbreak

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — wait for the laboratory reports before any action: Waiting allows many more people to fall ill

C — hand out medicines to all the families at once: Handing out medicines without finding the cause does not stop the outbreak

D — close the village well and leave: Closing the source without knowing whether it is the cause leaves the real source open

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The line list with the name, the age, the date of onset and the source of water of every case is sent to the health authority, since the pattern in the list is what points to the common source
option_1: visit the houses, take the history of each case, examine the patients and inspect the source of drinking water
option_2: wait for the laboratory reports before any action
option_3: hand out medicines to all the families at once

question: On the vaccine vial monitor of a vial of oral polio vaccine the square inside the circle is darker than the circle. This means that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the vial must be discarded because the vaccine has been exposed to heat

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The monitor darkens with the total heat to which the vial has been exposed, and once the square is darker than the circle the vaccine has lost its power and is thrown away

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the vial must be shaken and then used: Shaking does not restore a vaccine that has been spoilt by heat

B — the vial is safe and may be used as usual: Using such a vial gives no protection while the child believes he is immunised

C — the vial must be kept in the refrigerator and used tomorrow: Cooling cannot bring back the power that has been lost

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads the monitor and not the expiry date when the choice is between the two, and the discarded vials are entered in the vaccine tally sheet, since that record explains the difference between the vials received and those used
option_1: the vial must be shaken and then used
option_2: the vial is safe and may be used as usual
option_3: the vial must be kept in the refrigerator and used tomorrow
option_4: the vial must be discarded because the vaccine has been exposed to heat

question: The dose of a medicine for a child is best worked out according to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the weight of the child in kilograms, as the formulary directs

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The dose is worked out per kilogram of body weight, since children of the same age differ greatly in size and the weight is the figure that matters for the drug in the body

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — half the adult dose for every child: Half an adult dose may be far too much for a small child and too little for a large one

B — the height of the child alone: Height by itself does not decide the dose

D — the age of the child in years only: Age alone gives a rough and often unsafe figure

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The child is weighed on the same scale at every visit and the weight is written in the case sheet in kilograms, since a dose worked out on an old weight loses its value when the child has grown
option_1: half the adult dose for every child
option_3: the weight of the child in kilograms, as the formulary directs
option_4: the age of the child in years only

question: A 5-year-old child with a temperature of 104 degrees Fahrenheit suddenly becomes stiff and then jerks all over. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. turn the child to the side, loosen the clothing, protect from injury, give oxygen and give the prescribed antipyretic

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The sideways position keeps the airway clear, and protecting the child from the bed rails while giving oxygen and lowering the fever is what the fit needs

🔍 Key Clues: 5-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — wrap the child in a thick blanket: A thick blanket raises the temperature further

B — give a hot drink at once: A hot drink cannot be swallowed during a fit and may be inhaled

C — put a spoon between the teeth: A spoon may break the teeth and block the airway

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse notes the time the fit began and ended and what the child did during it, since a fit lasting more than fifteen minutes or one that starts on one side of the body calls for a change in treatment
option_1: wrap the child in a thick blanket
option_4: turn the child to the side, loosen the clothing, protect from injury, give oxygen and give the prescribed antipyretic

question: The site preferred for an intramuscular injection in a 3-year-old child is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. outer part of the thigh or the ventrogluteal site

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The outer thigh and the ventrogluteal area hold enough muscle in a small child and are free of large nerves and vessels

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — inner side of the arm: The inner side of the arm carries nerves and vessels close to the surface

B — upper outer part of the buttock: The buttock is not used in a small child, as the muscle is thin and the sciatic nerve lies close by

D — front of the thigh near the knee: The front of the thigh near the knee has little muscle and lies over the bone

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse holds the child firmly and explains the injection to the mother, since a child who moves at the wrong moment is the commonest reason for a needle to strike the bone or a nerve
option_3: outer part of the thigh or the ventrogluteal site
option_4: front of the thigh near the knee

question: The structure that prevents food from entering the windpipe during swallowing is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. epiglottis

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The epiglottis folds over the opening of the windpipe as the food is swallowed and so keeps it out of the airway

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — uvula: The uvula hangs from the soft palate and takes no part in closing the airway

C — soft palate: The soft palate closes off the nose during swallowing

D — vocal cord: The vocal cords lie inside the voice box and are not the flap that closes the opening

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse feeds a patient who has had a stroke with the head raised and checks that the swallow is clear, as the reflex that closes the epiglottis is often lost in such patients and the food then reaches the lung

question: The valves in the veins of the legs serve to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. keep the blood moving towards the heart and stop it from running back

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The valves open in the direction of the heart and close behind the column of blood, so that the muscle pump of the leg pushes the blood upwards

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — add oxygen to the blood as it passes: Oxygen is added in the lungs and not in the veins

C — filter the waste products out of the blood: Waste products are removed by the kidneys and the liver

D — slow the flow of blood in the veins: The valves do not slow the flow but keep it in one direction

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: A patient who stands for long hours is advised to wear support stockings, since the column of blood presses on valves that become weak with age and the legs then swell by the evening
option_1: add oxygen to the blood as it passes
option_2: keep the blood moving towards the heart and stop it from running back
option_3: filter the waste products out of the blood
option_4: slow the flow of blood in the veins

question: The part of the kidney that concentrates the urine is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. loop of Henle

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The loop of Henle builds up the concentration of salts in the tissue around it, and the water that is drawn out leaves the urine concentrated

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — urethra: The urethra carries the urine out of the bladder

C — renal pelvis: The renal pelvis collects the urine and passes it into the ureter

D — urinary bladder: The bladder stores the urine until it is passed

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: A patient whose urine output falls is asked about how much he is drinking and about any vomiting or loose motions, since the kidney can hold the water and pass concentrated urine until the shortage becomes severe

question: The defence mechanism in which a person refuses to accept a painful fact is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. denial

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In denial the mind keeps the painful information out of consciousness, as when a patient says that the report of his illness must be wrong

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — regression: In regression the person goes back to the behaviour of an earlier age

C — projection: In projection the person attributes his own feelings to another

D — sublimation: In sublimation an unacceptable urge is turned into something useful

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse does not argue with the patient at this stage, since the wall is a protection that comes down on its own as trust grows and the patient is ready to hear the truth

question: A patient who is to have an investigation asks the nurse the same question about the result several times in an hour. The best response is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. answer simply and truthfully every time, spend a few minutes with the patient and explain when the report is expected

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The repeated question is a sign of anxiety, and a calm truthful answer given without irritation with a few minutes of presence reduces it

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — tell the patient not to worry and change the subject: A change of subject makes the patient feel that he is being kept in the dark

B — say that the doctor will speak to him and walk away: Walking away makes the patient feel abandoned

C — tell the patient that asking again will not make the report come sooner: This reply is dismissive and adds to the anxiety

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse tells the patient the exact time the report is expected, since anxiety is greatest while the waiting has no clear end and it settles as soon as a time is fixed
option_1: tell the patient not to worry and change the subject
option_2: say that the doctor will speak to him and walk away
option_3: tell the patient that asking again will not make the report come sooner
option_4: answer simply and truthfully every time, spend a few minutes with the patient and explain when the report is expected

question: A patient with advanced kidney disease is advised to restrict the foods that are rich in:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. potassium

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A kidney that is not working cannot pass potassium out of the body, and a high level stops the heart, so bananas, coconut water, orange juice and salt substitutes are limited

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — iron: Many of these patients are short of iron and are given a supplement

C — fibre: Fibre is encouraged to avoid constipation

D — vitamin C: Vitamin C in the usual amounts is not harmful

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse also warns the patient against salt substitutes sold as low sodium products, since most of them are made largely of potassium and look harmless on the label

question: At the end of a shift the nurse in charge finds a shortage of a controlled drug in the cupboard. She should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. record the shortage at once, inform the nursing superintendent and the pharmacy, and check the register with the two nurses who signed it

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A shortage of a controlled drug is a serious matter that must be reported without delay so that the entries of the shift and the stock can be checked while the details are fresh

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — correct the figures in the register to match the stock: Altering the register is falsifying a record and is a serious offence

C — wait for the next shift to report it: Delay gives time for the facts to be forgotten and the blame to fall on the wrong person

D — replace the missing amount from the stock of another ward: Borrowing from another ward hides the loss and spreads the error

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The register is kept with the stock and both are checked and signed by the outgoing and the incoming nurse together, since a count that is signed at the bedside leaves no doubt about the handover
option_1: correct the figures in the register to match the stock
option_2: record the shortage at once, inform the nursing superintendent and the pharmacy, and check the register with the two nurses who signed it
option_3: wait for the next shift to report it
option_4: replace the missing amount from the stock of another ward

question: A null hypothesis in a study states that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. there is no difference between the groups being compared

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The null hypothesis says that any difference found between the groups is due to chance alone, and the study is designed to see whether it can be rejected

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the treatment under study is better than the other: That is the alternative or research hypothesis

C — the study will certainly be successful: A hypothesis is a statement to be tested and not a promise of success

D — all the patients will recover: The recovery of every patient is an outcome and not a hypothesis

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: Stating the null hypothesis before the study begins keeps the nurse researcher from reading a difference into the figures simply because the collected data are expected to show one
option_1: the treatment under study is better than the other
option_2: there is no difference between the groups being compared

question: According to Maslow, the need that is met immediately after the physiological needs is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. safety and security

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Once food, air, water and rest are secured, the person looks for safety and freedom from danger, which is why a frightened patient asks about his illness before he asks for food

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — esteem: Esteem comes above love and belonging

B — love and belonging: Love and belonging come after safety

D — self actualisation: Self actualisation is at the top of the ladder

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse arranges the care in this order, since a patient who is cold, thirsty or afraid cannot take in teaching about diet and drugs and must be settled first

question: A family in which a newly married couple lives in the home of the husband's parents is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a patrilocal family

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In a patrilocal arrangement the couple settles with or near the husband's parents, which is the common pattern in many parts of India

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a matrilocal family: A matrilocal family is one in which the couple lives with the wife's parents

B — a nuclear family living alone: A nuclear family living alone settles in a home of its own

C — a neolocal family: A neolocal family sets up a new home in a new place

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse asks who takes the decisions in the home before giving advice on diet or immunisation, as advice that the elders have not heard is often not followed however good it is

question: The head office of the International Council of Nurses is situated at:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Geneva

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The International Council of Nurses, the world body of nursing associations, has its headquarters at Geneva in Switzerland

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — New York: New York is the seat of the United Nations and of UNICEF

B — London: London is the home of the International Council of Nurses' older offices and of the Commonwealth Nurses Federation

D — The Hague: The Hague is the seat of the International Court of Justice

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The Council speaks for nurses at the world level on safe staffing and on the working conditions, which is why its statements are quoted when a nursing association negotiates with a government

question: The head office of the United Nations Children's Fund is located at:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. New York

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The United Nations Children's Fund has its headquarters in New York, in the United States of America

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Paris: Paris is the seat of UNESCO

B — Vienna: Vienna is the seat of the International Atomic Energy Agency

D — Rome: Rome is the seat of the Food and Agriculture Organization

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The Fund supplies the vaccines, the oral rehydration salts and the growth charts used in the child health programme, so the nurse who reads a carton in the labour room is handling material supplied through this agency

question: The Pradhan Mantri Bharatiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana is meant to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. supply good quality medicines at low prices through special outlets

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The scheme runs special outlets where generic medicines of assured quality are sold at prices far below the market rate

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — give a pension to the aged: Pensions are given by social welfare schemes

C — build new operation theatres: Construction of operation theatres is funded by the health infrastructure programmes

D — provide free spectacles to school children: Spectacles are provided under the school health programme

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse tells a patient on long term treatment where the nearest outlet is, since a patient who cannot afford the full course stops the drug half way and returns with a relapse
option_1: supply good quality medicines at low prices through special outlets

question: The Trained Nurses Association of India was founded in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 1908

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Trained Nurses Association of India was founded in 1908 and is one of the oldest professional nursing bodies in the country, working for the welfare and the standards of nurses

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1920: 1920 is the year the Indian Red Cross Society was established

B — 1905: 1905 is earlier than the founding of the association

C — 1947: 1947 is the year of Indian independence, long after the association began

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The association publishes the Nursing Journal of India and speaks for nurses on pay, safety and standards, so every nurse should know the body that represents the profession

question: Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram looks after the health needs of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. adolescents between ten and nineteen years

🧠 Clinical Rationale: This programme was started for the age group of ten to nineteen years and deals with nutrition, mental health, injuries, substance use and reproductive health

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — adults above sixty years: Older people come under the programme for the elderly

B — children below five years: Children below five years come under the child health programme

D — pregnant women only: Pregnant women are covered by the maternal health programme

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse holds adolescent friendly sessions in the school and the Anganwadi, since this age group rarely comes to the health centre on its own and the anaemia found at this time is easy to correct

question: The Kilkari scheme makes use of the mobile telephone mainly to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. send recorded health messages to pregnant women and mothers of young children

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The scheme delivers recorded messages with advice on care during pregnancy, delivery and infancy to the telephone of the mother at fixed intervals

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — locate the nearest hospital: Finding a hospital is not the purpose of the messages

C — call the doctor during an emergency: Emergency calls are made by the family and are not part of the scheme

D — collect money for treatment: No money is collected through this scheme

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse registers the telephone number of the mother in the system at her first visit, since the messages reach only those whose numbers have been entered and the advice is then repeated at home between visits
option_2: send recorded health messages to pregnant women and mothers of young children

question: The Employees' State Insurance Scheme provides medical care and cash benefit to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. workers in covered factories and establishments and their dependants

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The scheme covers insured workers of the establishments that come under it and gives them and their families medical care and cash benefit during sickness, maternity and injury at work

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — all persons below the poverty line: Families below the poverty line are covered by the public health system and by other schemes

C — persons above sixty five years only: Age alone does not decide membership of this scheme

D — government officers only: Government officers have their own service rules and a separate health scheme

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse in an industrial dispensary checks the insurance card of the worker before the treatment is recorded, since the entries on the card are the proof that the benefit was given and the worker's wages are paid accordingly
option_1: workers in covered factories and establishments and their dependants

question: The first Five Year Plan of India gave the highest priority to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. agriculture and irrigation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The first plan, which began in 1951, put agriculture and irrigation first because the country was short of food and the plan had to settle the immediate needs

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — defence production: Defence production was not the leading aim of the first plan

B — heavy industry: Heavy industry was the thrust of the second plan

D — information technology: Information technology came many years later

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The plan also supported the health services through the community development blocks, and it is from this period that the pattern of the primary health centre that the nurse still works in took shape

question: The vitamin present in abundance in the Indian gooseberry (amla) is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. vitamin C

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Indian gooseberry is one of the richest natural sources of vitamin C, and it keeps this vitamin even when it is dried

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — vitamin A: Vitamin A comes from the yellow and orange fruits and vegetables and from milk

C — vitamin D: Vitamin D is formed in the skin by sunlight

D — vitamin B 12: Vitamin B 12 comes from foods of animal origin

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse suggests the fruit to a family that cannot afford the tablets, since the local and cheap source is taken far more often than a bottle of medicine

question: The instrument used to measure the pressure of the atmosphere is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. barometer

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A barometer measures the pressure of the atmosphere and is used in the reading of the weather and in the calibration of the instruments of the ward

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — altimeter: An altimeter measures the height above sea level

C — hygrometer: A hygrometer measures the humidity of the air

D — anemometer: An anemometer measures the speed of the wind

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Each instrument is read with the unit in which it is scaled, since a pressure written down without its unit is of no use to the doctor who has to act on it

question: The blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. pulmonary artery

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The pulmonary artery is the only artery that carries blood poor in oxygen, and it takes the blood from the right side of the heart to the lungs

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — pulmonary vein: The pulmonary vein is the only vein that carries blood rich in oxygen, from the lungs back to the heart

B — superior vena cava: The superior vena cava brings deoxygenated blood from the upper part of the body to the heart

C — aorta: The aorta carries oxygenated blood to the whole body

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who takes a blood sample for a blood gas test uses an artery and not the pulmonary vessels, since it is the arterial blood that shows how well the lungs are working

question: The gland that is called the master gland of the body is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. pituitary

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The pituitary lies at the base of the brain and its hormones control the working of several other glands, which is why it is called the master gland

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — thymus: The thymus belongs to the immune system and is large in childhood

C — adrenal: The adrenal glands respond to the pituitary hormone and to stress

D — thyroid: The thyroid is controlled by the pituitary and controls the rate of metabolism

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: A patient with a pituitary problem is measured for height and watched for changes in the output of urine, as the same gland also controls the water balance of the body

question: The enzyme in the saliva that begins the digestion of starch is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. salivary amylase

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Salivary amylase begins to change starch into sugar in the mouth itself, which is why a piece of bread becomes sweet when it is chewed for some time

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — trypsin: Trypsin acts on proteins in the small intestine

B — pepsin: Pepsin acts on proteins in the stomach

C — lipase: Lipase acts on fats

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who gives a starch digestion test tells the patient to chew the sample well and to keep time, since the reaction in the mouth is what the test measures

question: The pH of the contents of an empty stomach is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 2.0

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The stomach secretes hydrochloric acid and its contents are strongly acidic, in the range of about one and a half to three

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 6.0: 6.0 is a weak acid such as milk or saliva

C — 7.4: 7.4 is the reaction of blood

D — 8.5: 8.5 is alkaline and is found in the small intestine

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Aspirate from a nasogastric tube that is acidic confirms that the tube lies in the stomach, and this is why the nurse tests the pH of the aspirate before every feed

question: The formed elements of the blood that are chiefly responsible for clotting are the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. platelets

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The platelets stick to the torn edge of the vessel and join with the clotting factors to form the plug that stops the bleeding

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — lymphocytes: Lymphocytes are one kind of white cell and have no part in clotting

B — red cells: The red cells carry oxygen and take no active part in making the plug

C — white cells: The white cells defend the body against infection

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: A patient whose platelet count is low is watched for small bleeds in the gum and under the skin, since the count must fall a long way before bleeding appears on its own

question: The radioisotope used in the treatment of cancer of the thyroid gland is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. iodine 131

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The thyroid takes up iodine from the blood, so radioactive iodine is carried to the gland and destroys the overactive or cancerous tissue from inside

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — cobalt 60: Cobalt 60 is used as an external source of radiation for other cancers

C — phosphorus 32: Phosphorus 32 is used in some blood disorders

D — technetium 99: Technetium 99 is used for pictures of the skeleton and other organs

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps the patient's urine and other body fluids away from pregnant staff and visitors for the time laid down, since the patient is passing radiation for a few days after the treatment

question: A dose of 500 milligrams expressed in grams is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 0.5 g

🧠 Method: One gram is a thousand milligrams, so five hundred milligrams is five hundred divided by a thousand, that is half a gram

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 50 g: 50 g equals fifty thousand milligrams

B — 5 g: 5 g equals five thousand milligrams

C — 0.05 g: 0.05 g equals only fifty milligrams

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse converts and writes the unit on the chart every time, since a decimal point placed wrongly in this conversion gives a dose ten times too large or too small

question: A patient is prescribed 60 mg of a drug and the tablets available are of 15 mg each. The number of tablets to be given is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 4

🧠 Method: Sixty divided by fifteen gives four, so four tablets make up the prescribed dose

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 3: Three tablets would give forty five milligrams

B — 2: Two tablets would give only thirty milligrams

C — 6: Six tablets would give ninety milligrams, which is an overdose

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse checks whether the tablets are scored before planning to break them and asks the pharmacist if no suitable strength is in stock, since a dose that has to be cut into three is a common source of error

question: Five tablets cost ₹37.50. The cost of a strip of ten tablets of the same medicine is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. ₹75.00

🧠 Method: One tablet costs thirty seven and a half divided by five, that is seven rupees fifty, and ten of them cost seventy five rupees

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — ₹70.00: Seventy rupees works out to seven rupees a tablet

C — ₹90.00: Ninety rupees is far more than the working gives

D — ₹80.00: Eighty rupees works out to eight rupees a tablet

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse helps a patient work out the monthly cost of a long term medicine, since a patient who sees the total in advance plans the purchase of a whole strip instead of buying a few tablets at a time at a higher rate

question: A nurse works eight hours a day for twenty six days in a month. The total number of hours worked is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 208

🧠 Method: Eight multiplied by twenty six gives two hundred and eight hours

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 218: 218 is higher than the product of the two figures

C — 186: 186 comes from multiplying eight by twenty three and a quarter

D — 198: 198 comes from multiplying eight by about twenty five

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The same working out is used when the nurse in charge prepares the duty roster, as the hours of every nurse are added at the end of the month to show that the laid down hours were not exceeded

question: A patient's fluid intake during a shift was 250 mL of tea, 200 mL of water and 150 mL of soup. The total intake in litres is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 0.60 litre

🧠 Method: The three amounts add up to six hundred millilitres, which is six hundred divided by a thousand, that is zero point six litre

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 0.45 litre: 0.45 litre equals four hundred and fifty millilitres

C — 1.20 litre: 1.20 litres would need a further six hundred millilitres

D — 0.75 litre: 0.75 litre equals seven hundred and fifty millilitres

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse adds the intake at the bedside at the end of every shift and not from memory the next morning, since an intake that is written up late is the commonest reason for a wrong fluid balance chart

question: Five hundred millilitres of a five per cent dextrose solution contains how much dextrose?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 25 g

🧠 Method: A five per cent solution has five grams in every hundred millilitres, so five hundred millilitres contain five multiplied by five, that is twenty five grams

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 10 g: 10 g would be the content of two hundred millilitres

B — 50 g: 50 g would be the content of a ten per cent solution of the same volume

C — 5 g: 5 g is the amount in one hundred millilitres

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse reads the strength printed on the bag and not the shape or the colour of the bag, since a ten per cent bag looks like the five per cent one and the two are stocked in the same store

question: A ward has forty patients and five nurses on the morning shift. If the nurse to patient ratio is to be one to six, the number of nurses still required is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 2

🧠 Method: Forty patients need about seven nurses at a ratio of one to six, and since five are already on duty, two more are required

⚡ Fast Approach: Add the parts to get the total number of parts, then find the value of one part.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 3: Three more would take the number well above the required figure

C — 1: One more would leave the ratio at about one to seven

D — 4: Four more would give nine nurses for forty patients

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse in charge writes the number of nurses needed against the number available for each shift, since this record is the evidence used when more staff are requested

question: Hand is to glove as foot is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. sock

🧠 Method: A glove is worn over the hand as a covering, just as a sock is worn over the foot

⚡ Fast Approach: State the relationship in words first, then look for the same relationship.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — shoe lace: A shoe lace is a part of the shoe and is not worn over the foot as a covering

B — toe: A toe is a part of the foot

D — ankle: The ankle is a part of the body and not a covering

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: In these pairs the nurse looks for the same relation between the two words rather than a meaning that merely sounds familiar, since the first answer that comes to mind is not always the one that fits the pattern

question: The next number in the series 5, 10, 20, 40 is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 80

🧠 Method: Each number is twice the one before it, and twice forty is eighty

⚡ Fast Approach: Check the differences first, then squares, cubes or multiplication.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 60: Sixty comes from adding twenty, which does not follow the pattern

B — 100: One hundred would be reached by adding sixty

C — 70: Seventy comes from adding thirty

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse checks the whole series before naming the next figure, since a pattern that holds for the first two pairs and breaks in the third is a trap in both this test and the reading of a chart

question: If A is 1, B is 2 and so on, the numbers that stand for the word CAT add up to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 24

🧠 Method: C is the third letter, A is the first and T is the twentieth, and three plus one plus twenty gives twenty four

⚡ Fast Approach: Compare the first and last letters of the given pair to find the shift.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 20: Twenty is the value of T alone

B — 22: Twenty two leaves out the first letter

D — 26: Twenty six is the number of letters in the alphabet

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Adding the values carefully is the same habit that keeps the nurse safe in a drug calculation test, where the total must be worked out step by step and checked rather than guessed

question: In a queue of twenty five people for the outpatient counter a nurse is seventh from the front. The number of people behind her is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 18

🧠 Method: The people behind her are the total less the seven at her place or in front of it, so twenty five minus seven gives eighteen

⚡ Fast Approach: Positions add up to one more than the total number in the row.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 19: Nineteen comes from subtracting six from twenty five

C — 17: Seventeen comes from subtracting eight from twenty five

D — 16: Sixteen leaves out two of the people behind her

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The same subtraction tells the nurse how many people are still waiting before the clinic closes, which is what the doctor is told before the last patient is taken in

question: Which of the following is the odd one out: 8, 27, 64, 100, 125?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 100

🧠 Method: All the others are perfect cubes of whole numbers, namely two, three, four and five, while one hundred is a perfect square but not a cube

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 27: 27 is the cube of three

B — 8: 8 is the cube of two

D — 64: 64 is the cube of four

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: When a single value does not fit a pattern, the nurse repeats the observation before acting, since a wrong reading copied into the chart is a bigger error than the reading itself

question: The angle between the two hands of a clock showing three o'clock is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 90 degrees

🧠 Method: Each hour on the dial covers thirty degrees and the hands are three hours apart, so the angle is three multiplied by thirty, that is ninety degrees

⚡ Fast Approach: Use the remainder after dividing by 7 for days, and 30 degrees per hour for clocks.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 60 degrees: Sixty degrees is the angle when the hands are two hours apart

C — 45 degrees: Forty five degrees is half of a right angle and does not correspond to a whole hour

D — 30 degrees: Thirty degrees is the angle when the hands are one hour apart

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: A sense of angles and position is what the nurse uses while positioning a patient in bed, since a limb placed at the wrong angle is a common cause of pressure and of nerve injury

question: If today is Monday, the day of the week after sixty one days will be:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Saturday

🧠 Method: Sixty one divided by seven leaves a remainder of five, and counting five days ahead of Monday gives Saturday

⚡ Fast Approach: Use the remainder after dividing by 7 for days, and 30 degrees per hour for clocks.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Monday: Monday would come after a multiple of seven days, such as sixty three days

B — Sunday: Sunday would be six days ahead

C — Friday: Friday would be four days ahead

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: Counting the days in this way is used while planning the next visit of a patient on a fixed day of the week, as a date worked out wrongly means that the patient waits at home for a nurse who is not coming
